name: Yuhyun Lee
status: Open to postdoctoral and neurotechnology R&D opportunities
hero_intro: a Ph.D. candidate in Biomedical Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University, advised by Prof. Pulkit Grover. My work brings together experimental neuroscience and engineering to develop and evaluate neural interfaces.
hero_body: My doctoral research focuses on transnasal electrical stimulation in mice, combining nasal electrode arrays with depth-resolved electrophysiology to understand stimulation-evoked responses across brain regions.
meta_description: Yuhyun Lee is a Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. candidate at Carnegie Mellon University building preclinical neural stimulation and electrophysiology platforms.
about_paragraph_1: I began by creating EEG tools for zebrafish and moved into electrical stimulation and multi-channel neural recording in mice. Working across models has shaped how I think about the strengths—and limits—of each experimental approach.
about_paragraph_2: Previously, I developed EEG recording systems for adult and larval zebrafish. I am particularly interested in research that connects preclinical platforms, neural signal analysis, and translational neurotechnology.
conference_text: IEEE BRAIN Discovery and Neurotechnology Workshop · Society for Neuroscience (SfN), Washington, DC
contact_body: I welcome conversations about postdoctoral research, neurotechnology R&D, and collaborations in neural interfaces, stimulation, and electrophysiology.
